messages.subject: merging the NSP & STY chip data for the 500k
parts:
Dear Sir/Madam,

I'm not sure whether somebody has asked the similar question before or
not... Is there any function that aroma provides for merging the CNV
regions detected by the NSP & STY chips? or could you provide some
information that how people usually deal with them please?

Thank you very much and look forward to any message from you.

I don't know of any particular method (statistical or algorithms) for
merging CN regions. Personally, I would merge the raw CN estimates
*before* (not after) running segmentation, CNV analysis etc. The
GladModel and CbsModel are examples doing this.

Cheers

messages.author: b9d1a0ccaae43087
messages.subject: Re: merging the NSP & STY chip data for the 500
parts:
Hi there,

I read your post, by a complete random sequence of events. The problem
that you are asking emerged at our department as well. I have created
a standalone program that combines the fragments/CNVs from both the
Affymetrix NSP and STY chips. The input for the program comes from the
Affymetrix genotyping console (downloadable from affy’s website).
If you are still interested in this problem you could contact me on my
e-mail and I could send you the program.
The program uses the sample ID (contains chip position- i.e. NPS or
STY), Gain or Loss, N markers, Start linear position, End linear
position and Chromosome. All these parameters are coming from the
Genotyping console, but this text file could be created from any
program. You could also specify a number of parameters in my program:
KB overlap between the two chips for each sample ID, maximum position
if no overlap (use it or not), minimum position if overlap (use it or
not), Start position (minimum or maximum), End position (minimum or
maximum) and you could export the result into a file.

If you are interested you could contact me, via e-mail:
Ivan...@cf.ac.uk

Regards,
Dobril Ivanov
Cardiff University/ Biostatistics and Bioinformatics Unit
